summary: 研究者尝试通过正念和注意积极经历来培养幸福感，新西兰学校也开展了相关课程。文章把参与者的体验与神经科学证据分开，讨论哪些改变已经观察到，哪些脑部解释仍待验证。

paragraphs.brief: 大卫森认为受过训练的大脑与未经训练的大脑在生理上是不同的
sentences: A psychiatrist Tony Fernando was walking down the street when he saw a group of young homeless men sitting on the footpath.
一名精神病医生Tony Fernando在街上走着，当时他看到一群无家可归的年轻人坐在路上。
As Fernando handed out gifts of food, he tried to video the men’s reactions in his mind, recording how their gratitude lifted him in return.
费尔南多把食物送给别人时，他试图在脑海中录制这些人的反应，记录他们的感激感动他。
‘I felt warm, content, meaningful,’ he says.
他说：「我觉得温暖、满足、有意义。
Fernando believes the brain can be trained to make us happy and that his ‘video method’ is one way to achieve this.
费尔南多认为大脑可以被训练来让我们快乐他的“视频方法”是达到这个目的的一种方法
In fact, a growing body of scientific research internationally is showing how we can learn happiness in the same way we can learn to play the piano.
事实上，越来越多的国际科学研究正在展示我们如何学习快乐以同样的方法，我们可以学习弹钢琴。
In the soft tissue that forms the brain, there are approximately ten trillion synapses connecting roughly a hundred billion neurons.
在形成大脑的软组织中，大约有10万亿个突触连接了大约1000亿个神经元。
Active synapses become more sensitive; less active synapses die, but new ones grow quickly.
活动突触变得更加敏感；活动较不活跃的突触死亡，但新的突触迅速增长。
This is relatively new thinking – just 30 years ago, neuroscientists believed that adult brain cells couldn’t regenerate.
这是相对较新的想法 - 仅仅在30年前，神经科学家相信成人脑细胞无法再生。
One of the pioneers in this field is University of Wisconsin professor Richard Davidson.
这一领域的先驱之一是威斯康辛大学教授理查德·戴维森。

He studied Buddhist monks using brain scans in his research facility, and found that those trained in meditation had higher levels of activity in the left prefrontal cortex – the area associated with happiness.
他研究佛教僧侣时，在他的研究设施里使用脑部扫描，发现那些受过冥想训练的人在与幸福相关的左前额皮层的活动水平更高。
Davidson believes that the trained brain is physically different from the untrained one.
大卫森认为受过训练的大脑与未经训练的大脑在生理上是不同的

paragraphs.brief: 如果你一直沉浸在自我批评和担忧上他争辩说你的大脑会因此成形
sentences: The idea that we can train our brains to find more happiness has been called ‘mindfulness’ by neuropsychologist Rick Hanson, author of Hardwiring Happiness.
我们能够训练大脑、体会更多幸福感。神经心理学家、《重塑幸福》一书的作者里克·汉森将这种做法称为“正念”。
It was in college that Hanson, quite unintentionally, first recognised the importance of something that would become his life’s work.
汉森在大学里无意中首先认识到成为他一生工作的东西的重要性
As an unconfident teenager, he discovered he could turn a small event, ‘a young woman smiling at me’, into a good feeling he could hold on to.
他发现自己可以把一个小事件“一个年轻女人对我微笑”，变成他可以抱持的良好感觉。
To do this, Hanson employs exactly the same imaginary ‘video method’ as psychiatrist Tony Fernando.
汉森使用完全相同的假想“视频方法”作为心理医生Tony Fernando。
‘The brain takes its shape from what the mind rests upon,’ says Hanson.
汉森说，“大脑的形状来自思想所依赖的东西”。
If you keep resting your mind on self-criticism and worries, he argues, your brain will be shaped by that.
如果你一直沉浸在自我批评和担忧上他争辩说你的大脑会因此成形

Hanson explains that resting it on pleasant feelings and the things you have accomplished means that over time your brain will take on a different shape, with strength and optimism hard-wired into it.
汉森解释说把它放在愉快的感情上你所完成的事情意味着你的大脑会逐渐变形

paragraphs.brief: 他发现，使用多种幸福途径的人取得了最佳结果，这表明平衡胜于集中关注你最认同的单一途径。
sentences: In New Zealand, the Mental Health Foundation runs mindfulness programmes in 14 schools.
在新西兰，心理健康基金会在14所学校开展了提高认识方案。
Foundation CEO Judi Clements says, ‘It’s a valuable approach because children are told to pay attention, but aren’t told how to pay attention.’
基金会首席执行官Judi Clements说，“这是一个很有价值的方法，因为儿童们被告知要注意，但是他们却没有被告知要注意。”
Preliminary results on the outcomes found that children had sustained increases in well-being.
有关成果的初步结果发现，儿童的福祉持续提高。
The Foundation recognises five pathways to happiness – being active, connecting with others, taking notice, learning and giving.
基金会认识到实现幸福的五条途径 — — 积极与他人联系、注意、学习和给予。
And, says Clements, ‘We’re detecting a hunger for it from different organisations and professions as well, so the Foundation is soon going to pilot an online “well-being game” in several workplaces.’
并且Clements说，`我们发现不同组织及专业都渴望这个游戏，因此基金会很快将在多个工作场所试行网上“健康游戏 ”。
The project leader is psychologist Carsten Grimm, who is interested in whether some pathways to happiness are more effective than others.
项目领导人是心理学家Carsten Grim，他对一些通往幸福的途径是否比其他途径更有效感兴趣。
In a study, Grimm recorded the activities and corresponding happiness scores of 173 people.
在一项研究中，格林记录了173人的活动和相应的幸福分数。
What he found was that people who used several pathways to happiness achieved the best results, suggesting it’s better to have a balance than concentrate on the single pathway you most identify with.
他发现，使用多种幸福途径的人取得了最佳结果，这表明平衡胜于集中关注你最认同的单一途径。

paragraphs.brief: 然而，心理医学副教授Nathan Consedine 以疲惫的叹息迎接我们坚持不懈地寻找幸福的秘密。
sentences: However, Associate Professor of Psychological Medicine Nathan Consedine greets our relentless search for the secrets to happiness with a tired sigh.
然而，心理医学副教授Nathan Consedine 以疲惫的叹息迎接我们坚持不懈地寻找幸福的秘密。
‘The more you chase it, the less you get it,’ he says, quoting studies showing those who value contentment and well-being are, in fact, less happy.
他说，引用一些研究，显示那些重视满足和福利的人，其实是不太快乐的：“你追得越多，就越少。”
The big question, he says, is whether there’s any benefit in actively seeking happiness.
他说，最大的问题是积极寻求幸福是否有好处。
He cites a study, for example, which showed that people who were happier were less inclined to show sympathy.
例如，他引用了一项研究，该研究表明，那些更快乐的人不太愿意表示同情。

Consedine says that’s probably because happy people are strongly motivated to stay happy, but engaging sympathetically with others typically involves engaging with their distress, and that’s going to reduce their own happiness.
康西丁认为，这大概是因为快乐的人很想保持愉快，而同情他人通常意味着要体会对方的痛苦，这会减弱他们自己的快乐感。
Consedine’s not disagreeing with the theory of mindfulness, but believes there’s more work to be done.
康塞丁并不不同意谨慎的理论，但认为还有更多的工作要做。

paragraphs.brief: 其中一些工作正在奥克兰大学脑部研究中心进行。
sentences: Some of that work is being conducted at Auckland University’s Centre for Brain Research.
其中一些工作正在奥克兰大学脑部研究中心进行。
Associate Professor Johanna Montgomery has been studying Hanson’s theory – that altering our brain activity at a synaptic level affects our behaviour.
副教授约翰娜・蒙哥马利一直在研究汉森的理论改变我们的大脑活动影响我们的行为
She accepts that it’s a logical explanation based on studies from animals, but we haven’t yet got the technology to prove it scientifically in humans.
她承认这是基于动物研究的逻辑解释但是我们还没有技术来科学地证明人类的存在
It’s true that MRI scans certainly do indicate an increased flow of blood to different areas of the brain which are experiencing positive stimuli.
确实，核磁共振扫描确实表明血液流向大脑中正经历积极刺激的不同区域。
However, she warns that this is a long way from confirming that the brain itself is developing or strengthening.
然而，她警告说，这远远不能证实大脑本身正在发展或增强。

paragraphs.brief: 更清楚的是长期恐惧对大脑活动的影响，而不是生命中积极事件释放出来的“幸福”激素的影响。
sentences: Nonetheless, Montgomery believes she is making progress.
然而，蒙哥马利认为她正在取得进展。

In the laboratory, when scientists want to experiment with synaptic connections, they stimulate the brain with electricity, as this copies the high-frequency firings that happen normally in the brain every second.
在实验室里，当科学家们想要实验神经连接时，他们用电刺激大脑，因为这复制了大脑中通常每秒发生的高频点火。
Using this technique, Montgomery has made a number of findings.
Montgomery利用这一技术得出了一些结论。

For example, the hormones that are released routinely in response to good or bad situations – such as adrenaline – act to regulate the brain, in the same way that weather has a regulating effect on human activity more generally.
例如，针对好坏情况(如肾上腺素)而定期释放的荷尔蒙，可以调节大脑，就像天气对人类活动产生调节效应一样。
But scientists understand some of these stimuli better than others.
但是科学家们比其他人更了解这些刺激因素。
More is known about the impact on brain activity of prolonged periods of fear than the effects of ‘happiness’ hormones that are released by positive events in life.
更清楚的是长期恐惧对大脑活动的影响，而不是生命中积极事件释放出来的“幸福”激素的影响。
This is one potentially important area that she hopes to investigate further in future.
这是她希望今后进一步调查的潜在重要领域。

items.en: a reference to a fact that two scientists use the same technique to promote their own happiness
items.zh: 提到一个事实两位科学家使用同样的技术来增进他们自己的幸福
items.why: 汉森与精神科医师费尔南多都用想象中重放积极经历的“录像”方法提高自己的幸福感。

items.en: the suggestion that scientific opinion about an aspect of brain function has changed over a given time period
items.zh: 有关大脑功能的一个方面的科学意见在特定时期内发生了变化的建议
items.why: 文章把三十年前认为成年脑细胞无法再生的看法与较新的认识对照，显示科学观点发生转变。

items.en: an estimate of how numerous some brain components are
items.why: “approximately/roughly”=估计。对象是突触和神经元数量。

items.en: the reason why some educational courses were set up
items.zh: 开设某些教育课程的原因
items.why: 学校常要求孩子集中注意力，却没有教他们怎样集中注意力，这正是设立正念课程的理由。

items.en: It’s better to look for a variety of ways to increase happiness than focus on just one.
items.zh: 寻找多种方式来增加幸福比只关注一个更好。

items.en: Focusing on personal achievements rather than negative experiences will make people happier.
items.zh: 注重个人成就而不是消极经历，将使人民更加幸福。

items.en: Happy people might have a reason not to display one favourable characteristic.
items.zh: 快乐的人可能有理由不表现出一个有利的特征。

items.en: A range of groups are becoming more interested in learning techniques to improve happiness.
items.zh: 一系列群体对学习提高幸福感的方法越来越感兴趣。

items.en: Auckland University’s Centre for Brain Research Associate Professor Johanna Montgomery says that current research into brain activity and behaviour only relates to ________, so Hanson’s theories have not been proved correct.
items.zh: 奥克兰大学脑研究中心副教授约翰娜·蒙哥马利指出，目前有关脑活动与行为的研究只涉及________，因此汉森的理论尚未得到证实。
items.why: 现有研究只与动物有关，因此 Hanson 的理论尚未被在人类上证明。

items.en: While scans do show that positive stimuli result in more ________ reaching parts of the brain, this isn’t proof that the brain is getting stronger.
items.zh: 扫描确实显示，正面刺激会使更多________流向大脑某些区域，但这不足以证明大脑正在变得更强健。
items.why: 扫描显示积极刺激使更多血液到达大脑各区。

items.en: In laboratory experiments, scientists use ________ to initiate brain activity, because it’s similar to natural processes.
items.zh: 在实验室里，科学家用________引发脑活动，因为这种刺激与自然发生的过程相似。
items.why: 实验中用电来启动脑活动，因为它类似自然过程。

items.en: One finding is that hormones can be compared to the ________, because both can change human behaviour.
items.zh: 一项发现是，激素可以与________相比，因为两者都能改变人的行为。
items.why: 激素可与天气类比，二者都能改变人类行为。

items.en: But scientists understand some stimuli, such as ________, better than they understand more positive stimuli.
items.zh: 不过，与较为正面的刺激相比，科学家对某些刺激了解更多，例如________。
items.why: 科学家更了解恐惧等刺激的作用，而非更积极的刺激。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

points: 学校常要求孩子集中注意力，却没有教他们怎样集中注意力，这正是设立正念课程的理由。
现有研究只与动物有关，因此 Hanson 的理论尚未被在人类上证明。
clauses: This is relatively new thinking – just 30 years ago, neuroscientists believed ….
“that adult brain cells couldn’t regenerate”补足 believed 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 believed 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
…, he argues, your brain will be shaped by that.
连接词 if 引出“If you keep resting your mind on self-criticism and worries”，说明主句的条件关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 if 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: Some recent developments in the science of happiness
幸福科学的一些最新发展
